title: A Weekend Phone Call
description: Four phone conversations about weekend plans: shopping, a message from Grandma, a family party and a restaurant booking.
instructions: Read the questions for each part first. Then press Play and listen. Choose the best answer (A, B or C) for each question.

parts.title: Part 1 · Plans with a friend
parts.intro: You will hear Hoa phoning her friend Jack about the weekend.

script.speaker: Hoa
script.text: Hi, Jack. It's Hoa. Are you busy this weekend?

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: Hi, Hoa! Well, on Saturday morning I have football practice, but I'm free in the afternoon.

script.speaker: Hoa
script.text: Great. Do you want to come shopping with me? I need a present for my mum. It's her birthday on Sunday.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: Sure. What does she like?

script.speaker: Hoa
script.text: She loves flowers and she likes reading, so maybe a book. I can't decide.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: A book is a better idea. Flowers die after a few days.

script.speaker: Hoa
script.text: True! OK, so can we meet at two o'clock at the bookshop on Park Street?

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: Two is a bit early. My practice finishes at twelve, but then I need to have lunch and a shower. Can we say three?

script.speaker: Hoa
script.text: Fine, three o'clock. And after that, shall we see a film?

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: Good idea. But I don't have much money this month, so nothing expensive.

script.speaker: Hoa
script.text: No problem. I'll pay for the tickets, and you can buy the ice cream.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: Deal! See you on Saturday.

parts.title: Part 2 · A message from Grandma
parts.intro: You will hear a voicemail message from Tom's grandmother.

script.speaker: Grandma
script.text: Hello, Tom, it's Grandma. I hope you're well. I'm calling because I'd like you to come for lunch on Sunday, if you're free. Your cousins are coming too.

script.speaker: Grandma
script.text: I'm making your favourite, chicken soup, and there is a big chocolate cake. Well, I didn't buy it, I made it myself, of course!

script.speaker: Grandma
script.text: Could you bring your guitar? Your little cousin Ella wants to hear you play. And please ask your mum if she can bring some fruit.

script.speaker: Grandma
script.text: Lunch is at one o'clock, but come at half past twelve if you can, because I need help in the garden. The apples are ready, and I can't reach the high branches. Please don't forget your boots, because it was raining all week and the garden is very muddy.

script.speaker: Grandma
script.text: Oh, and my phone isn't working well. If you want to call back, use the house phone, not my mobile.

script.speaker: Grandma
script.text: I'm looking forward to seeing you. Lots of love. Bye bye!

parts.title: Part 3 · Brother and sister
parts.intro: You will hear Linh phoning her brother Minh, who is at university.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Hi, Minh! How's university?

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: Hi, Linh. It's tiring, honestly. I have two exams next week, so I'm studying all weekend.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Oh no. I was hoping you could come home on Saturday. It's Dad's fiftieth birthday party.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: I know, I know. I feel terrible, but I really can't come. Maybe I can take the train on Sunday morning.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: That's too late. The party is on Saturday evening. Mum says if you take the early train on Saturday, you'll be here by noon.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: Hmm. The exam is on Monday, and I haven't finished my project.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Why don't you bring your books home? You can study in your old room. It's quiet, and Mum will cook for you.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: That's actually a good idea. Then I don't need to waste time cooking. Okay, I'll catch the nine o'clock train.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Wonderful! Dad will be so happy. But keep it a secret. He doesn't know you're coming.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: My lips are sealed. What shall I get him?

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Don't worry. I've already bought a present from both of us. You can pay me back later.

parts.title: Part 4 · Booking a restaurant
parts.intro: You will hear Peter phoning a restaurant to book a table.

script.speaker: Anna
script.text: Good evening, Blue Garden Restaurant. Anna speaking.

script.speaker: Peter
script.text: Hello. I'd like to book a table for Saturday evening, please.

script.speaker: Anna
script.text: Certainly. How many people?

script.speaker: Peter
script.text: Six. No, sorry, seven. My sister's boyfriend is coming too.

script.speaker: Anna
script.text: And what time?

script.speaker: Peter
script.text: Half past seven, please.

script.speaker: Anna
script.text: I'm afraid we're full at that time. I can offer you a table at seven, or at nine.

script.speaker: Peter
script.text: Seven is fine, but could we sit outside? It's my mum's birthday and she loves the garden.

script.speaker: Anna
script.text: Of course, if it doesn't rain. If it does, we'll move you inside. Can I take a name?

script.speaker: Peter
script.text: It's Collins, Peter Collins.

script.speaker: Anna
script.text: Thank you. Do you have any allergies or special food needs?

script.speaker: Peter
script.text: My dad can't eat fish, and my sister is vegetarian.

script.speaker: Anna
script.text: No problem. I'll tell the chef. Shall I add a birthday cake?

script.speaker: Peter
script.text: Yes, please! That's a lovely idea. How much is it?

script.speaker: Anna
script.text: It's ten pounds for a small cake, and we put a candle on top.

script.speaker: Peter
script.text: Perfect. Thank you!
